sections.name: Brand Voice Pillars
sections.why: Five pillars, each with all four sub-fields filled and examples cited to named pages (why-testlify, walmart-hiring-process, makipeople-alternatives). Every Avoid list ends in a runnable check ('every claim of improvement carries a number or a named source', 'could a lawyer sign off on the sentence?'), not sentiment. Fairness language stays at 'reduce bias' / 'level playing field' with absolutes explicitly banned.

sections.name: Tone Guidelines
sections.why: General tone persona is concrete and grounded in site lines; all four content-type variations present, each with exactly four quoted example phrases that read as sourced blog/product copy, not generic filler.

sections.name: Messaging Framework
sections.why: Five messages, each with Title/Concept/Key Points/Usage; key points are verbatim quotes with pages named (screening-in-vs-screening-out, testlify-vs-testgorilla, pricing). One internal wobble worth fixing at leisure: Message 2 says '4,000+ roles' while Pillar 2 says '4,500+ roles' — reconcile to the real site figure. Not a gate failure since both are specific, sourced-register numbers, but one of them is wrong.

sections.name: Value Propositions
sections.why: Six real segments (SMB, enterprise/high-volume, technical, blue-collar, compliance, non-profit), each specific with product facts (45+ languages, Walmart's 500,000/yr). The ⚑ HUMAN DECISION flag on staffing agencies is legitimate honesty about missing evidence, not a gap.

sections.name: Writing Style Guidelines
sections.why: All four sub-blocks present with ~4 rules each; Terminology carries six Say-This→Not-That pairs, each with a reason. The one numeric rule with no observed evidence (average sentence length) is correctly ⚑-flagged rather than invented. Rules are checkable ('never run three same-length sentences in a row'), not vibes.

sections.name: Content Formatting
sections.why: Headlines, Subheadings, Lists, and CTAs all present with real observed patterns and exact site button text ('Try for Free', 'Book a Demo', 'View sample questions'). The headline character cap is ⚑-flagged as ungrounded instead of fabricated — correct handling.

sections.name: Voice Examples
sections.why: Two verbatim ✅ excerpts with source pages named (why-testlify, walmart-hiring-process), each with five specific 'Why this works' bullets. The ❌ example is explicitly labeled as constructed, and its five failure bullets tie each flaw back to what the real voice does instead, including the 'eliminates bias' legal trap.

sections.name: Audience Understanding
sections.why: Primary audience plus four secondary audiences, five priorities, five pain points, and five serving principles — all anchored in quoted site language and real numbers (42 days, 87% skills gap, named ATS integrations), not category-generic personas.

sections.name: Quality Checklist
sections.why: Exactly ten checkboxes, each a runnable yes/no test tied to the document's own pillars and terminology rules, plus a 'Remember:' line built from the site's real tagline.
